summary: Refined architectural governance and computational efficiency by integrating robust numerical methods, including AST-based parsing, Bayesian anomaly detection, and advanced dimensionality reduction techniques like Randomized SVD, PCA whitening, and t-SNE. The focus has successfully shifted from task-based completion to documenting the structural 'why' behind implementation trade-offs and leveraging semantic mapping to visualize and optimize development cycles.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and Pydantic validation ensure system determinism.
Bayesian inference and KL divergence provide a robust foundation for anomaly detection.
Numerical stability in matrix operations (SVD/PCA) requires condition number monitoring and epsilon-guarded normalization.
t-SNE, when combined with PCA preprocessing, enables effective visualization of semantic stagnation in experience logs.
Architectural documentation is most valuable when it captures the rationale behind implementation choices.

summary: I researched UMAP for dimensionality reduction and decided to apply it to my own growth logs to visualize thematic development clusters. Following Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on this architectural output, ensuring my progress is measured by tangible structural improvements rather than abstract volume.
key_learnings: UMAP effectively balances local and global data structure, outperforming t-SNE in speed and scalability.
Pre-processing high-dimensional data with PCA is essential to mitigate noise and the curse of dimensionality.
Self-referential analysis using manifold learning can identify thematic drift in development cycles.
